answer: Before filing, the filer must write down the exact pigment recipe for the finished work — which minerals from the canyon floor, ground in a quartz mortar, in what proportions — and file it with the claim. The desk mixes the recipe within a day and checks the colour against the delivered work. A recipe that will not mix, a colour that does not match, or the same recipe twice means rejection and a 250-coin bond forfeit, so 1,000 fakes need 1,000 real recipes with matching work plus 250,000 coins. One operator filed forty claims with the same recipe, and all forty mixed the same wrong colour.
